gen-dafont-joystix-gf-onest: Arcade swagger lives in Joystix, with its widely tracked letters and stems barely thicker than the arms they join. Onest follows with short ascenders and big bowls, and a long run of text would glide along in one smooth, wire-like line.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-open-sans: Open Sans brings bulky lowercase and curves that never clog, modern and easygoing. Open Sans next to Joystix, with its bold arcade tracking, gives the page one loud voice and one that simply carries the words.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-oxygen: Joystix is bold arcade lettering, spaced wide, with a compact gap between x-height and ascender line. And Oxygen takes over the text, its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, so nudge its size up a notch for comfort.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-pathway-extreme: Joystix hits hard with bold arcade lettering, its horizontals lighter than the stems but never threadlike. Pathway Extreme does the quiet work, with stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height and rounded letters that stay clearly open.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-puritan: Joystix goes for bold arcade punch, with widely tracked lettering and heavy stems easing into slightly lighter curves. But Puritan handles the sentences, its rounded forms staying open and its oversized e and a counters keeping each word approachable.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-saira: Joystix is all bold arcade attitude, widely tracked, with curves that thin only modestly where they turn. Then Saira steps in, its rounded letters stretching toward the top line and each s open enough to see through.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sen: Joystix sounds like an arcade cabinet, bold and widely tracked. Sen settles into text with tall lowercase and a cable-like line of constant weight, so paragraphs would run smooth and modern, with curved strokes ending before they turn inward.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sofia-sans: Tall, rounded lowercase with one open side and no thick-thin shift make Sofia Sans read like cut acrylic stencils. Joystix does the loud arcade shouting with widely tracked letters, while Sofia Sans simply carries the sentences.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-stack-sans-notch: Joystix brings bold arcade lettering with a gentle ebb and flow in its stroke weight. Stack Sans Notch has rod-stock verticals and horizontals and a big-bodied lowercase, so you can let its size run a little smaller without losing presence.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-stack-sans-text: Upstrokes and downstrokes in Joystix differ by only a faint amount, yet its widely tracked, arcade-bold lettering still jumps off the screen. Stack Sans Text counters with marker-like constant lines and big-bodied lowercase, and that sturdy simplicity is the pair's best quality.
